headline: One second slower.

scenes.say: You turn your watch back one second, and every day on Earth gets one second longer.
At midnight, every clock in a hospital downtown starts disagreeing with every other clock.
A day with a leap second really has 86,401 seconds instead of 86,400.

visual.head: THAT'S REAL
visual.text: seconds in a day with a leap second

scenes.say: And one extra second has broken real computers. In 2012, Qantas and Mozilla reported problems.

visual.head: THAT'S REAL
visual.text: Qantas, Mozilla and Linux sites hit

scenes.say: So you try to turn the watch forward again, and the crown won't move.
The second hand starts turning backward on its own. Full video on the channel.

seo.summary:
Full video: https://youtu.be/<id>

Turn a watch back one second and the whole Earth spins slower. One extra second sounds harmless, but a day with a leap second has 86,401 seconds, and the June 2012 leap second caused software problems at Qantas, Mozilla and many Linux sites. A fictional What If story with real facts (timeanddate.com, Wikipedia 'Leap second').

forbattring.problem: TLI:s långa videor får ~0 exponeringar; Shorts gav LS/STE/QM nästan all tidig trafik (TITTARTID_REGLER v48).
forbattring.andring: DISTRIBUTIONSORDER 2: titel med sökfrasen + #shorts, EN vändning (en extra sekund kraschar datorer, verkligt 2012), länk till långa videon först i beskrivningen, cliffhanger (kronan fast).
forbattring.forvantat: ≥ 300 visningar i Shorts-flödet på 48 h och klick till den långa videon.
forbattring.referens: QM-Shorten 22/11 och TLI-Shorten 22/11 (samma mall: en vändning + 'Full video on the channel').
forbattring.vi_slår_den_med: Två verkliga fakta på 30 s (86 401 sekunder, Qantas/Mozilla 2012) och en tydlig cliffhanger som bara långa videon löser.
